rationale: This profile is a tiny (1801 text bytes, 5 functions), float-intensive benchmark suite whose hot paths are the numeric loops in advance, energy, and main, so the table prioritizes transforms with strong per-instruction obfuscation value and low loop-body overhead while penalizing anything that bloats the very small binary or sits inside inner loops. SUB gets the highest diversity weight since arithmetic substitution is cheap, correct, and especially effective on the dense FP/integer constant math here. SPLIT is favored (near-zero runtime cost, high diversity for tiny functions like _start and offset_momentum) as the most efficient way to fragment a 827-byte main. FLA carries high SecurityGain but its runtime/size costs are kept high-weight to restrain application in the hot numeric loops and in this size-critical binary. BCF is heavily penalized on runtime and size because bogus control flow multiplies both in exactly the inner-loop code that dominates this suite, so it should apply sparingly. ICALL is moderately penalized on runtime (indirect-call overhead in hot paths) but remains attractive on diversity since direct call patterns in a 5-function program are trivial to read. IGV and IBR get balanced mid-range weights: inter-block and register-global tricks add meaningful reverse-engineering friction with acceptable cost given the small function count, and modest correctness-risk weights on IGV/ICALL/BCF let the feature-driven selector avoid them where FP-heavy code could be perturbed.
